metadata.content: Scott Parker to West Ham: Can former Hammers player roll back years and win Premier League promotion yet again? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Scott Parker to West Ham: Can former Hammers player roll back years and win Premier League promotion yet again? Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Wednesday 4 November 2026 10:21, UK Image: Scott Parker is in the West Ham hotseat As soon as news of Nuno Espirito Santo's departure was announced, only one name seemed to make sense for West Ham. The Hammers want to get out of the Championship. They need someone who has taken a relegated Premier League side back into the top flight in style. Scott Parker has done both on several occasions. At Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, the former England international achieved tickets to the promised land with all three. Parker dealt with the high expectations of all three clubs and delivered on his promises. United and Carrick looked dead and buried within the first 18 minutes as the Italian side took a two-goal lead in the early exchanges. It prompted boos and protests from supporters, who threw tennis balls onto the pitch, but the Red Devils turned things around as a Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha double gave them their first win in 54 days. metadata.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday.
metadata.content: Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat Jodie Burrage has revealed online abuse and death threats; both Burrage and fellow British player Katie Boulter believe most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing Wednesday 4 November 2026 08:29, UK Image: Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday. Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months, went down against India's Vaishnavi Adkar. She looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes. The 27-year-old, who reached a career-high ranking 85 in September 2023, published an Instagram story with some of the abuse received due to the defeat.
